ldn-57.name: Barnard 68
ldn-57.introduction: is a small cloud of gas and dust about 500 light-years away in Ophiuchus, so dense that it blots out every star behind it in visible light. It is a Bok globule, a compact dark cloud that can collapse into a new star. It is also catalogued as LDN 57.

image.alt: A black, starless hole in a dense field of stars, with reddened stars around its edge.
image.caption: ESO · VLT, visible and near-infrared composite · released 2001
image.credit: ESO. VLT/FORS1 visible and near-infrared composite, released January 2001. Resized to 600 × 600 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESO: How to become a star

sections.title: Mapped by 3,700 stars
sections.text: In 2001, astronomers measured how much the cloud dims about 3,700 stars behind it, over 1,000 of them visible only in infrared light. That mapped the dust inside with a precision of about 3%. The cloud holds about twice the mass of the Sun at only 16 K (−257 °C).

source.title: ESO: How to become a star (eso0102)

sections.title: A star in waiting
sections.text: Barnard 68’s sharp edges show that it is on the verge of gravitational collapse, and it may become a star within the next 200,000 years or so. Until then its outer layers wobble like a water-filled balloon that has been jiggled.

cahlon-cloud-30.name: Coalsack
cahlon-cloud-30.introduction: is a cloud of dust about 600 light-years away that blots out a patch of the Milky Way beside the Southern Cross, easily seen with the naked eye. It covers about 7 by 5 degrees, the area of well over a hundred full Moons, and reaches into Centaurus and Musca. It is also catalogued as Caldwell 99.

image.alt: A dark, starless lane across a dense Milky Way star field beside the bright star Acrux.
image.caption: ESO/Digitized Sky Survey 2 · visible-light survey composite · released 2015
image.credit: ESO/Digitized Sky Survey 2. Acknowledgment: Davide De Martin. Visible-light survey composite, released October 2015. Resized to 600 × 449 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESO: Wide-field view of part of the Coalsack Nebula

sections.title: The emu’s head
sections.text: Many cultures see the Coalsack as a dark constellation. In several Aboriginal Australian cultures it is the head of the Emu in the Sky, and the Wergaia called it Tchingal. Inca astronomers named it Yutu, after a partridge-like bird, and on Bali it is Bubu Bosor, a leaky fish trap.

sections.title: The Black Magellanic Cloud
sections.text: Vicente Yáñez Pinzón gave the first European report of the Coalsack in 1499. Amerigo Vespucci called it “il Canopo fosco”, the dark Canopus, and it was also known as Macula Magellani or the Black Magellanic Cloud, a dark twin of the two bright Magellanic Clouds.

sections.title: Not quite black
sections.text: The Coalsack is not completely dark: a 1970 study found that it shines with about a tenth of the brightness of the surrounding Milky Way. Its dust grains, coated with frozen water, nitrogen and carbon monoxide, block blue light more than red, so the stars seen through it look redder than they are.

source.title: ESO: A Cosmic Sackful of Black Coal (eso1539)

cahlon-cloud-22.name: Taurus Molecular Cloud
cahlon-cloud-22.introduction: is possibly the nearest large stellar nursery, about 480 light-years away in Taurus and Auriga. Its dark lanes shelter hundreds of newborn stars only about 1–2 million years old. It is also known as Heiles’s Cloud 2.

image.alt: Dark, branching lanes of dust across a star field, with a small glowing nebula near the center.
image.caption: Keesscherer · visible light · 2017
image.credit: Keesscherer. Visible light, September–December 2017. Resized to 600 × 464 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: Wikimedia Commons: Taurus Molecular Cloud 1 and IC 2087

sections.title: A chemistry lab in the dark
sections.text: No other place in space has yielded more newly discovered molecules. Over 100 kinds have been found in the cold gas of its core TMC-1, from long carbon chains to ring molecules such as indene. In 2007, the carbon-chain ion C₈H⁻ found here became only the second kind of negative molecular ion known in interstellar space.

sections.title: Where T Tauri stars got their name
sections.text: The variable star T Tauri, the prototype of young Sun-like stars, belongs to the cloud’s family. So does HL Tauri, whose planet-forming disk has been imaged in striking detail, and V1298 Tauri, a young star with four transiting planets. Being so close and so rich in young stars, the cloud is ideal for studying how planets form.

ldn-66.name: Snake Nebula
ldn-66.introduction: is a thin, S-shaped lane of dust about 500 light-years away in Ophiuchus, silhouetted against the dense star clouds near the center of the Milky Way. It winds out from the edge of the bowl of the Pipe Nebula. It is also catalogued as Barnard 72 and LDN 66.

image.alt: A thin, dark S-shaped lane winding across a dense golden star field, with small dark clouds below it.
image.caption: Friendlystar · visible light
image.credit: Friendlystar. Visible light. Resized to 600 × 600 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A dark snake for small telescopes
sections.text: The lane is only 2–3 arcminutes thick, so a good view needs a 4–6 inch telescope and clear, dark skies. It shares its patch of sky with Barnard 68 and the small dark clouds Barnard 69, 70 and 74.

ldn-1746.name: Barnard 59

source.title: ESO: Ceci n’est pas une pipe (eso1233)

ldn-1746.introduction: is the mouthpiece of the Pipe Nebula, a cloud of dust about 590 light-years away in Ophiuchus, silhouetted against the star clouds near the center of the Milky Way. It forms fewer stars than similar clouds, but faint wisps in its darkest part are lit by stars that are just forming. It is also catalogued as LDN 1746.

image.alt: Smoky dark clouds of dust in a dense star field, with a faint glow near the center.
image.caption: ESO · MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, visible light · released 2012
image.credit: ESO. Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, visible light, released August 2012. Resized to 600 × 561 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESO: The mouthpiece of the Pipe Nebula

sections.title: Barnard’s dark clouds
sections.text: E. E. Barnard was the first to record dark nebulae systematically with long-exposure photography, and he catalogued 370 of them all over the sky. Five of them make up the whole Pipe Nebula: Barnard 59, 65, 66, 67 and 78. Under dark, clear skies the Pipe is easy to see with the naked eye.

ldn-42.name: Barnard 78
ldn-42.introduction: is the bowl of the Pipe Nebula, a cloud of dust about 510 light-years away in Ophiuchus, silhouetted against the star clouds near the center of the Milky Way. It is also catalogued as LDN 42.

image.alt: A long, dark lane of dust shaped like a tobacco pipe across the rich star clouds of the Milky Way.
image.caption: ESO/Yuri Beletsky · visible light · 2009
image.credit: ESO/Yuri Beletsky. Visible light, 2009. Resized to 600 × 396 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

sections.title: A pipe in the Milky Way
sections.text: Barnard 59, 65, 66 and 67 form the stem, about 5 degrees long, and Barnard 78 the bowl. Under dark skies the Pipe is clearly visible to the naked eye and is best seen with 7× binoculars. It is itself part of the larger Dark Horse Nebula.

ldn-1551.name: LDN 1551

source.title: Fridlund (2016), My Favorite Object: L1551 IRS 5

ldn-1551.introduction: is a small, dense dark cloud about 480 light-years away in Taurus, whose young stars have been studied for more than 40 years. In 1980, the gas streaming from its hidden protostar IRS 5 became the first bipolar outflow ever found.

image.alt: Young stars glowing in blue haze, with orange gas around one of them and a bright jet at lower right.
image.caption: ESA/Hubble and NASA, Judy Schmidt · visible light · released 2014
image.credit: ESA/Hubble and NASA. Acknowledgement: Judy Schmidt. Hubble ACS, visible light, released November 2014. Resized to 600 × 581 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: ESA/Hubble: Jets, bubbles and bursts of light in Taurus

sections.title: The first bipolar outflow
sections.text: Ronald Snell, Robert Loren and Richard Plambeck mapped carbon monoxide in the cloud and found two lobes of gas, one approaching and one receding, on opposite sides of IRS 5. They span more than 20 arcminutes on the sky. IRS 5 turned out to be a pair of protostars, each with a disk the size of the Solar System, and its jets reach more than 500 km/s.

sections.title: A disk seen edge-on
sections.text: HH 30, in the same cloud, is the prototype of an edge-on planet-forming disk. The young star is hidden behind its own disk, while a fast jet shoots out at right angles inside a wider, cone-shaped outflow. Webb images released in February 2025 show the disk and jet in unprecedented detail.

source.title: ESA/Webb: Webb investigates a dusty and dynamic disc

cahlon-cloud-20.name: Musca and Chamaeleon Molecular Cloud
cahlon-cloud-20.introduction: is a group of dark clouds about 600 light-years away in the far southern constellations Chamaeleon and Musca, at the surface of the Local Bubble. Its Chamaeleon I cloud is one of the nearest active stellar nurseries, with 200–300 young stars.

image.alt: Blue haze and tangled dark and brown dust around young stars in the Chamaeleon I cloud.
image.caption: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA · Dark Energy Camera, visible light · released 2025
image.credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA. Image processing: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab). Dark Energy Camera, visible light, released June 2025. Resized to 600 × 540 and converted to AVIF; colors unchanged.

source.title: NOIRLab: The Ominous Chamaeleon I Dark Cloud

sections.title: A filament that is really a sheet
sections.text: The long, thin Musca cloud was long taken for a filament. In 2018, astronomers used the faint striations around it to measure how the cloud vibrates, and found the characteristic patterns of a sheet seen edge-on instead.

sections.title: The Dark Doodad
sections.text: Astrophotographers know the Musca cloud as the Dark Doodad, a name Dennis di Cicco gave it in 1986 after imaging it from Alice Springs. Aage Sandqvist had catalogued it in 1977, and the dark streak stretches nearly three degrees across the sky.

sections.title: Firsts in Chamaeleon I
sections.text: In 1998, Cha Hα 1 in Chamaeleon I became the first brown dwarf seen in X-rays. The cloud also holds OTS 44, an object with only the mass of a planet that is surrounded by a disk of its own.

cahlon-cloud-0.name: MBM 12
cahlon-cloud-0.introduction: is a small molecular cloud well away from the plane of the Milky Way, about 920 light-years away in Aries. It shelters a group of young stars only about 2 million years old.

sections.title: The nearest cloud that wasn’t
sections.text: Earlier estimates put MBM 12 only 160–330 light-years away, which would have made it the nearest molecular cloud to the Sun. In 2001, Kevin Luhman compared faint red dwarfs in front of and behind the cloud and moved it to about 900 light-years, outside the Local Bubble of hot gas around the Sun.

cahlon-cloud-7.name: Orion B Molecular Cloud
cahlon-cloud-7.introduction: is one of the giant molecular clouds of the Orion complex, about 1,320 light-years away. It holds some of Orion’s best-known sights: the Horsehead Nebula, the Flame Nebula and the reflection nebula Messier 78.

sections.title: Nurseries in the dark
sections.text: Several star-forming regions lie inside the cloud. The largest is the cluster within the Flame Nebula, part of Orion’s youngest group of stars, less than 2 million years old. Jets from newborn stars light up Herbig–Haro objects such as HH 24–26 and HH 111, and McNeil’s Nebula, a variable nebula near Messier 78, was discovered in 2004.
